title: Bousfield–Kan replacements: invariance and diagonal comparison
statement:
Use simplicial sets and the simplex category $\Delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $C$ be a small category and $X:C\to\mathrm{sSet}$ a diagram. Define simplicial sets $\mathrm{BK}_C X$ and $\mathrm{KB}_C X$ by
$$
(\mathrm{BK}_C X)_r=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_r}X(c_0)_r,\qquad
(\mathrm{KB}_C X)_r=\coprod_{c_r\to\cdots\to c_0}X(c_r)_r.
$$
Faces delete an endpoint or compose adjacent arrows and apply the matching face of $X$; when deleting the endpoint carrying the element, first apply $X$ to its adjacent arrow. Degeneracies insert identities and apply the matching degeneracy of $X$. Both constructions are functorial in $X$ and in reindexing functors $u:C'\to C$. An objectwise weak homotopy equivalence $X\to Y$ induces weak homotopy equivalences $\mathrm{BK}_C X\to\mathrm{BK}_C Y$ and $\mathrm{KB}_C X\to\mathrm{KB}_C Y$. For a bisimplicial set $Z:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ define its diagonal by $(\operatorname{diag}Z)_r=Z_{r,r}$, with each simplicial operator acting in both variables. For every such $Z$ there are natural weak homotopy equivalences $\mathrm{BK}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}Z\to\operatorname{diag}Z$ and $\mathrm{KB}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}Z\to\operatorname{diag}Z$. These comparison maps in degree zero take the summand indexed by $[0]$ identically to $Z_{0,0}$.

source.place: Zhen Lin Low, Revisiting function complexes and simplicial localisation (2014), Definition 1.1, Lemmas 1.3–1.4, pp. 3–5. No Stacks tag states this homotopical result.

proof.text: Separate the two simplicial directions: put $B(X)_{p,q}=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_p}X(c_0)_q$ and $T(X)_{p,q}=\coprod_{c_p\to\cdots\to c_0}X(c_p)_q$. In the $p$ direction use composition/deletion and identity insertion, applying $X$ when deleting the element-carrying endpoint; in the $q$ direction use the operators of $X$. The $p$ identities follow from associativity, identities and functoriality of $X$; the two directions commute because every $X(a)$ is a simplicial map. Thus these are bisimplicial sets and their diagonals are exactly the stated replacements. A transformation $X\to Y$ acts on the element, and a reindexing functor acts on the chain. Both commute with every operator by naturality and preservation of composition/identities, and respect identity and composite transformations/functors.

source.place: Definition 1.1, Remark 1.2 and Lemmas 1.3–1.4, pp. 3–5; explicit agent proof via simplex categories and diagonal invariance

proof.text: Fix $p$. The row map $B(X)_{p,\bullet}\to B(Y)_{p,\bullet}$ is the disjoint union, over the same set of chains, of the weak homotopy equivalences $X(c_0)\to Y(c_0)$. Realization is the quotient by simplex-operator relations, none of which change the chain label in this row, so its realization is the topological disjoint union of the corresponding realized maps. Path components are the disjoint union of components, and a based map from a connected sphere (and any based homotopy) stays in its one summand. Hence the map induces the required bijection of components and all homotopy-group isomorphisms. This also proves the analogous row assertion for $T$, with $c_p$ instead of $c_0$, including empty coproducts. These are exactly the weak equivalences defined in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Definition 1.1, Remark 1.2 and Lemmas 1.3–1.4, pp. 3–5; explicit agent proof via simplex categories and diagonal invariance

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to the two rowwise weak equivalences just proved. Their diagonals are the induced maps $\mathrm{BK}_C X\to\mathrm{BK}_C Y$ and $\mathrm{KB}_C X\to\mathrm{KB}_C Y$ from step 1, so this proves objectwise invariance for both replacements. No finiteness or fibrancy is assumed, and smallness of $C$ ensures that every indexing collection is a set.

source.place: Definition 1.1, Remark 1.2 and Lemmas 1.3–1.4, pp. 3–5; explicit agent proof via simplex categories and diagonal invariance

proof.text: For $Z$ fix its second degree $q$ and set $K=Z_{\bullet,q}$. The column $T(Z)_{\bullet,q}$ is $NE(K)$: an index chain in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ written $[n_p]\to\cdots\to[n_0]$ is a chain $[n_0]\to\cdots\to[n_p]$ in $\Delta$, and its element $x\in K_{n_p}$ determines every earlier simplex by restriction. This bijection commutes with all faces and degeneracies. The last-vertex map of [lem-coef-simplex-category-last-vertex] therefore gives $T(Z)_{\bullet,q}\to Z_{\bullet,q}$, a weak equivalence. Its formula on a $p$-chain is $K(v)x$ with $v(i)$ the image of the last vertex $n_i$ in $[n_p]$. The vertex assignment is monotone since $a_{i+1}(n_i)\leq n_{i+1}$ and all subsequent maps are monotone. Naturality of the cited theorem makes these maps commute with operators in $q$, so they assemble to a bisimplicial map $T(Z)\to Z$.

source.place: Definition 1.1, Remark 1.2 and Lemmas 1.3–1.4, pp. 3–5; explicit agent proof via simplex categories and diagonal invariance

proof.text: For the other replacement $B(Z)_{\bullet,q}=N(E(K)^{\mathrm{op}})$. A chain is $[n_p]\xrightarrow{f_p}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_1}[n_0]$ in $\Delta$, with $x\in K_{n_0}$. Define $u:[p]\to[n_0]$ by $u(i)=f_1\cdots f_i(0)$ and use $K(u)x$. The map $u$ is monotone since $f_{i+1}(0)\geq0$ and the earlier $f_j$ are monotone. To see this is a natural simplicial weak equivalence, let $K^{\mathrm{rev}}$ be obtained by reversing each simplex order: $a:[m]\to[n]$ becomes $a^{\mathrm{rev}}(j)=n-a(m-j)$. The functor fixing $([n],x)$ and sending an arrow $a$ to $a^{\mathrm{rev}}$ gives an isomorphism $E(K^{\mathrm{rev}})\cong E(K)$: its arrow condition is $K(a^{\mathrm{rev}})y=x$, and applying reversal twice is the identity. Reverse the nerve simplicial order too; $N(E(K))^{\mathrm{rev}}\cong N(E(K)^{\mathrm{op}})$. Under these identifications the reversed last-vertex map of [lem-coef-simplex-category-last-vertex] is precisely the displayed $u$ formula, since reversing a last vertex yields the first vertex $0$. Reversal preserves weak homotopy equivalences: the maps on realizations sending barycentric coordinates $(t_0,\ldots,t_p)$ to $(t_p,\ldots,t_0)$ respect every defining quotient relation and are mutually inverse homeomorphisms, natural in simplicial maps. Thus $B(Z)_{\bullet,q}\to K$ is a weak equivalence. Naturality in $K$ again assembles these maps into a bisimplicial map $B(Z)\to Z$.

source.place: Definition 1.1, Remark 1.2 and Lemmas 1.3–1.4, pp. 3–5; explicit agent proof via simplex categories and diagonal invariance

proof.text: The two maps of steps 4–5 are columnwise weak equivalences. Apply the exchanged-direction assertion of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence]. Their diagonal maps are the required $\mathrm{BK}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}Z\to\operatorname{diag}Z$ and $\mathrm{KB}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}Z\to\operatorname{diag}Z$. All chain identifications and vertex formulas commute with maps of $Z$, so the diagonal maps are natural. In degree zero on the summand $[n_0]=[0]$, both $u$ and $v$ are the identity $[0]\to[0]$; the resulting map on $Z_{0,0}$ is therefore the identity.
